newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinian airline makes inaugural flight to Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian airline makes inaugural flight to Saudi.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority's newly-established airline made an inaugural international flight on Friday carrying Palestinian pilgrims from Egypt to Saudi Arabia, an official said.
Two Palestinian Airlines planes took off from Port Said in northern Egypt within twenty minutes of each other early on Friday, the first day of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
The planes are bound for the Red Sea city of Jeddah, Mahmoud Ragab, general manager of the Port Said airport, told Reuters.
He said one plane carried 50 people and the other 45 passengers.
Saudi Arabia gave the green light on Thursday for the Fokker planes to make the inaugural flight on Friday morning, the chairman of the airline, Faiz Zaidan told Reuters.
"We have the green light from the Saudi Foreign Ministry at the highest level," he said on Thursday.

The two Fokker 50 aircraft took off from Port Said at 10:10 a.m. (0810 GMT) and 10:30 a.m. (0830 GMT), Ragab said. The Gazan pilgrims are due to perform the umra, or "minor pilgrimage", to the Moslem holy city of Mecca.
Five flights on the same route will follow, spread over Saturday, Sunday and Monday, Zaidan said.
The Palestinian Authority built its own airport in Gaza but the Israelis will not let Palestinians use it for regular flights.
It has received only two flights -- one carrying Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, the other a Moroccan plane bringing aid for the Palestinians, Zaidan said.
The airline, which is wholly owned by the civil aviation authority of the Palestinian Authority, will bring the same pilgrims back between January 21 and 23.
Fokker Aviation sold two second-hand Fokker 50 propeller jets to the Palestinian Authority in May, the first two aircraft to be bought by Palestinian Airlines.
